title: A branch for the summer sale

terminal.description: A shell in the top folder. Run the setup once to build the shop's folder, then go into shop and work there with git.

tasks.title: Make the branch summer-sale and switch to it
tasks.description:
Run `node setup.mjs` in the top folder, then work inside `shop`. The repository has one branch, `main`, with the site as it is today.

Make a new branch called `summer-sale`, starting from the last commit of `main`, and switch to it, so the next commits go onto it.

The check expects a branch with exactly that name that holds every commit of `main` from the setup, and you to be on it (or to have committed on it).
nextSteps: Run `git status`: its first line says `On branch main`.
Run `git branch` to list the branches. There is one.
Make `summer-sale` and switch to it, in one command or two.
Run `git status` again: the first line names the new branch.
hints: Making a branch and moving onto it are two separate things. A new branch starts from the commit you are on.
`git switch` moves you to a branch. One of its options makes the branch first.

tasks.title: Commit the sale on summer-sale
tasks.description:
On `summer-sale`, open `shop/index.html` and add this line just under the paragraph about Bramley Row, inside the page: ```

Summer sale: every book half price, 1 to 31 July.

``` Save it and commit it on `summer-sale`. Change no other file. The check looks for a commit on `summer-sale`, and not on `main`, whose home page announces the summer sale, and expects the other pages on `summer-sale` to be as they are on `main`.
nextSteps: Make sure `git status` says `On branch summer-sale`.
Add the line to `shop/index.html` in the editor and save.
Stage the file and commit it with a message that says what changed.
Run `git log --oneline -n 3`: your commit is at the top, on `summer-sale`.
hints: A commit goes onto the branch you are on. Check the first line of git status before you commit.
Committing on a branch is the same two steps as always: stage, then commit.
Run `git add index.html`, then `git commit -m "Announce the summer sale on the home page"`.

tasks.title: Switch back to main and see the sale go
tasks.description:
Switch back to `main`. Keep `shop/index.html` open in the editor: the sale line disappears, because `main` does not have that commit. It is still safe on `summer-sale`.

The check expects you to be on `main`, the sale to be committed on `summer-sale`, and `index.html` in the working folder to have no sale line.
nextSteps: Run `git status` first: there must be nothing left to commit.
Look at `shop/index.html` in the editor: the sale line is gone.
Run `git log --oneline --graph --all -n 4` to see both branches.
hints: Switching branches puts the files of that branch's last commit in the working folder.
The command that moved you onto summer-sale also moves you back, without its option.

tasks.title: Move the reading group to 19:00, on main
tasks.description:
The reading group cannot wait for July. Wilma wants it to meet at 19:00 instead of 18:30, on the site now. On `main`, open `shop/events.html`, change the time on the line about the first Thursday of the month, save, and commit it on `main`.

The check looks for a commit on `main` whose reading group meets at 19:00 and no longer at 18:30, expects every other line of that page to be as it was, and the sale to stay off `main`.
nextSteps: Make sure `git status` says `On branch main`.
Change only the time on the reading group line, and save.
Run `git log --oneline --graph --all -n 4`: the two branches now go different ways.
hints: This commit belongs on main, so check the first line of git status before you commit.
The sale is not in the files on main, so this commit cannot take it along.
Run `git add events.html`, then `git commit -m "Move the reading group to 19:00"`.
